MINUTES
  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  JULY 16, 2019

  A regular meeting of the Environmental Advisory Committee was called to order at 7:00 p.m. in
  the City Hall Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by CHAIR ZUCKERMAN.

  2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  BACINSKI, CHAN-SOUTHWELL,
  LARSON, RADOCCHIO, RETZ,
  SCHACHTER, ZUCKERMAN

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  STEGURA, NAVI

  STAFF PRESENT:  PLANNING MANAGER NAUGHTON,
  ADMINISTRATIVE ASSISTANT COREA

  3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  APPROVAL  OF  ENVIRONMENTAL  ADVISORY  COMMITTEE  MEETING
  MINUTES, APRIL 16, 2019

  In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER BACINSKI, Chair Zuckerman and
  Planning Manager Naughton provided information on the CPA budget which is available
  at https://cleanpoweralliance.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/FY-2019-20-Budget.pdf.
  Staff will send a link to the Committee.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER BACINSKI inquired about a program for residents similar to the
  Clean Bay program for restaurants. Chair Zuckerman stated that he will be attending a
  retreat soon and will inquire about developing such a program.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER BACINSKI inquired about the RFP for the Sustainability Update.
  Planning Manager Naughton stated that there was only one response to the RFP and
  SCAG is in the process of rewriting the RFP in hopes of getting a better response. Once
  the RFP is finalized, a copy will be provided to the Committee.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER BACINSKI moved, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
  SCHACHTER to,

  APPROVE THE ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES OF APRIL 16, 2019 AS PRESENTED.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN encouraged the Committee to visit the Los Angeles County
  website and review their recently finalized Sustainability Element.

  4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

  NONE

  5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A.  CLEAN BAY CERTIFIED RESTAURANT PROGRAM

  PLANNING MANAGER NAUGHTON provided a brief summary of the Clean Bay Certified
  Restaurant Program which is conducted by McGowan Consulting and the City’s Code
  Compliance staff. As of this meeting, there is only one restaurant to inspect out of the 38
  eateries in the City. Planning Manager Naughton provided information on the process.

  In response to a question by CHAIR ZUCKERMAN, Planning Manager Naughton stated
  that there are restaurants that need to be educated on better ways to prevent pollutants
  from getting into the storm drain.

   In response to a question by CHAIR ZUCKERMAN, Kathleen McGowan stated that the
  City does have the ability to impose fines, however, there has not been a need to do so in
  the City.

  A brief discussion ensued on this item.

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN received and filed this item.

  B.  STORM WATER QUALITY DESIGN GUIDELINES: RESIDENTIAL EQUESTRIAN
  FACILITIES

  Ms. Kathleen McGowan, McGowan Consulting provided a presentation to the Committee
  with a summary on the Storm Water Design Guidelines for residential equestrian facilities.

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN asked if “Round-Up” is a problem for the City with respect to
  Machado Lake or other receiving waters. Ms. McGowan stated that it could be a cause of
  aquatic life impairment but does not believe that there are long-term bio-concentration
  factors. She further stated that the California Stormwater Quality Association has done
  research on pesticide issues and it has been found that aquatic toxicity has been
  associated with the most recent version of pesticides.

  Ms. McGowan stated that the goal with treatment of the equestrian facilities is to retain or
  treat the runoff from the areas where horses are kept or maintained. She stated that there
  are links to resources for help with the design of biofilters/bioretention systems as well as
  native plant vegetation.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER RETZ stated that a presentation to the Dapplegray Lanes
  Homeowners Association would be helpful.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff is requesting direction from the Committee
  on the content and structure of the regulatory compliance component of the guidelines.
  A discussion ensued on this item.

  The Committee agreed that this should be required for new construction.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER RETZ suggested a cost effective option for one or two horses or
  come up with criteria for at what point a homeowner will be required to install an
  engineered system.

  In response to a question regarding the magnitude of the problem, Ms. McGowan stated
  that there were studies done calculating the number of horses and the amount of lawn
  area and determined that equestrian use and lawns likely have the same level of nitrogen
  and phosphorus damage.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER SCHACHTER expressed concern about why horse owners are
  not required to pick up after their horses on trails. COMMITTEE MEMBER RETZ agreed
  that this needs to be addressed.

  A discussion ensued on how to maintain the trails. (Staff will check with the City Attorney
  on private trails that have public access).

  Ms. McGowan stated that she agrees with COMMITTEE MEMBER RETZ idea to have a
  simple design option which does not require an engineered system. She suggested that
  for remodels the guidelines should be implemented depending on what is being changed
  on the facility (e.g. requiring gutters for barn reroofs).

  COMMITTEE MEMBER CHAN-SOUTHWELL inquired about the trail on PVDE adjacent
  to the Country Club. Planning Manager Naughton stated that there was a storm drain
  failure and there is a question on who is responsible for repairs. As soon as this is resolved
  the trail will be repaired and reopened.

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN inquired about housekeeping at Howlett Park. Ms. McGowan stated
  that an inspection was done at Howlett Park and suggestions for improvement were
  provided to the City.
  2
Environmental Advisory Committee,
Minutes, July 16, 2019
   In response to a question by CHAIR ZUCKERMAN, Ms. McGowan stated that there was
  an inspection done at Seacrest and Empty Saddle Club a number of years ago and the
  new design guidelines should be provided to them. CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that
  these are the types of facilities that should be phased in. Ms. McGowan stated that the
  City now has an equestrian facility that has been retrofit to use as an example.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER RETZ suggested that providing a copy of the survey could be
  useful information and also help educate homeowners on the guidelines.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER RADOCCHIO expressed concern on how to enforce these
  guidelines and inquired about rain gutters at stables. He added that rain gutters are not a
  big expense to install.

  Planning Manager Naughton summarized the discussion and stated that the following
  direction was provided to staff:

  ●  For existing single family residential, a simplified educational checklist/handout on
  treatment systems that can be provided to HOA’s, feed stores, and individual
  property owners, which can be provided through social media or e-mail blasts.

  ●  For new residential construction, develop criteria with focus on tying into major
  improvements, site design, and source control measures. As a last resort
  installation of bio-treatment systems.

  ●  For commercial municipal facilities, staff will research how best to approach the
  trails with the challenges of having private/public rings and trails.

  ●  Look into peacock resistant flowers and plants.

  ●  Cost effective ways to address channelized flow.

  ●  Add language for enforcement measures.

  ●  Cost of bio-treatment systems, however, this may be challenging due to the
  varying site constraints.

  The Committee agreed to continue this item to a future EAC meeting.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

  6.  STAFF ITEMS (Verbal Reports)

  A.  REGIONAL SUSTAINABILITY PLANNING EFFORTS

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that SCAG and the SBCCOG is preparing an
  adaptation  plan; the links will be provided to the Committee and encouraged anyone
  interested to participate in their online surveys.

  B.  CITY LANDSCAPE PESTICIDE USE

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the City Council has voted to cease the use of
  pesticides and herbicides in City maintained landscape areas. Bennet Landscaping is
  working on estimates for making this happen and the estimates will be brought to the
  City Council for discussion.

  C.  5G TELECOMMUNICATION FACILITIES IN PUBLIC RIGHT-OF-WAYS

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the City is limited by Federal and State Law on
  reviewing the 5G telecommunications facilities on aesthetics or on EMF and are also
  somewhat limited by their use in the City rights-of-ways.

  3
Environmental Advisory Committee,
Minutes, July 16, 2019
   COMMITTEE MEMBER BACINSKI inquired about other organizations that will look into
  the health risks. Planning Manager Naughton stated that it is the FCC and a memo from
  the City Attorney states that if an applicant demonstrates that the proposed facility will not
  exceed EMF limits regarding RF emissions, then the City cannot deny the application.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that she will include in an email to the Committee, a
  link to the SBCCOG’s Environmental Services Center with information and upcoming
  events.

  7.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  NONE

  8.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN adjourned the meeting at 9:02 p.m.

  The next Environmental Advisory Committee Meeting will be held on October 15, 2019
  at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos
  Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

  Respectfully submitted,

  ______________________________
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant
